plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Plump, ruffled blooms the size of a saucer open from fat buds, often in shades of shell pink with deeper rose centers. Many carry a sweet, rosy perfume. Whole borders of them look like scoops of sorbet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, from late May into June
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the northern hemisphere, including the central United States such as St. Louis, Missouri
plants.funFact: Peonies are among the longest-lived garden perennials. A single clump can bloom for decades, and some have outlived the people who planted them.

plants.name: Rhododendron ponticum
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs become mounds of lilac-purple trumpets, each throat freckled with golden-green spots. Large trusses of flowers light up woodland edges and estate gardens.
plants.location: Native to the Black Sea region and the Iberian Peninsula. Widely naturalized in Ireland and Britain.
plants.funFact: Plants flower only after about 10 to 12 years of growth. Each bloom is a long wait that pays off in a spectacular show.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, fragrant mounds send up slender spikes of tiny violet-blue flowers that hum with bees. The scent is clean, herbal and sweet. Blooms begin in early summer.
plants.location: Temperate gardens across Europe and North America, where flowering begins in early June
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin word for washing. Romans scented their baths with it.
